paragraphs.text: A traditional tower windmill turns the energy of the wind into a force that grinds grain. At the top of the tower sits a wooden cap, which can be turned so that the sails always face into the wind.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The four sails are attached to a horizontal shaft called the windshaft. As the sails turn, a large wheel on the windshaft drives a smaller gear connected to a vertical shaft running down through the tower.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: At the bottom of this shaft, the power is passed to a pair of heavy millstones. Grain is poured into a wooden hopper above the stones and falls slowly between them, where it is crushed into flour.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: The flour then travels down a chute into sacks on the ground floor. A miller could control how fine the flour was by adjusting the gap between the stones.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Many old windmills have now been restored, and some still produce small amounts of flour that are sold to visitors.
paragraphs.label: E
